query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled amount of lattice distortion through alloying elements with different atomic sizes can improve the combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance of a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Introduction of lattice distortion through alloying elements with different atomic sizes
generation.conditions: Alloy composition: Mg-rich with multiple principal elements; Processing conditions: induction melting or mechanical alloying; Test conditions: room temperature, cryogenic temperature, and high temperature (up to 900 °C)
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice distortion and formation of a simple solid solution phase instead of intermetallic compounds
generation.mechanism: Severe local lattice distortion can impede dislocation motion, leading to pronounced strengthening effect, while the formation of a simple solid solution phase can improve corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties (strength, ductility, and hardness), enhanced corrosion resistance, and improved high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy without lattice distortion
generation.boundary: Density below 6 g/cm3, alloy composition varying from 5 to 35 at% for each principal element
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of lattice distortion required to achieve optimal performance is uncertain and may depend on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with varying amounts of lattice distortion introduced through alloying elements with different atomic sizes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of lattice distortion does not lead to improved mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance, the hypothesis is falsified
